questions.question: The AI Centre of Excellence for Education announced in Union Budget 2025 is intended to benefit which sector the most?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The announcement of an **AI Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Education** in the **Union Budget 2025** (referring to the fiscal cycle of **2024-25**) is a core component of the "Make AI in India and Make AI Work for India" initiative.
 
• The primary objective of this centre is to revolutionize the **Education** sector by integrating **Artificial Intelligence** into teaching methodologies, personalized learning, and administrative frameworks. ***Hence, the option Education is correct.***
 
• These centres are designed to facilitate **interdisciplinary research** between top **Educational Institutions** and leading industry players to develop scalable AI solutions for the masses.
 
• By focusing on **Education**, the government aims to improve **learning outcomes**, reduce the dropout rate, and provide **data-driven insights** for curriculum reform.
 
• The initiative directly supports the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, which advocates for the extensive use of **Technology** in teaching and learning, especially in local languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sectoral CoEs:** While the focus here is on **Education**, the government has previously identified three specific areas for AI Centres of Excellence: **Agriculture**, **Health**, and **Sustainable Cities**.
 
• **Viksit Bharat @ 2047:** The integration of AI into **Education** is a stepping stone toward the goal of **Viksit Bharat** (Developed India) by the year **2047**, ensuring the youth are proficient in **New-age Technologies**.
 
• **Skilling Initiatives:** This aligns with the **Skill India Mission** and **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0**, which focuses on training students in **Coding**, **AI**, **Robotics**, and **Internet of Things (IoT)**.
 
• **Budgetary Focus:** The **Union Budget** presented by Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** has consistently increased the allocation for **Digital Infrastructure**, emphasizing the role of the **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)** in social sectors.
 
• **Research Corpus:** A massive corpus of **Rs. 1 lakh crore** has been proposed to provide long-term, low-interest loans for **Research and Innovation** in sunrise sectors, which includes **Educational Technology (EdTech)** and AI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Research Foundation (ANRF):** The **Anusandhan National Research Foundation** is another key body that works alongside these AI CoEs to provide high-level strategic direction for **Scientific Research** in India.
 
• **Personalized Learning:** AI in the **Education** sector is expected to enable **Adaptive Learning**, where the software adjusts the difficulty and style of content based on an individual student’s performance and **Learning Speed**.
 
• **Global Context:** India’s push for AI in **Education** places it among global leaders like the **USA** and **China**, who are also investing heavily in **Educational AI** to maintain a competitive **Human Resource** edge.
 
• **Implementation Date:** The framework for these centres was solidified during the **Full Union Budget 2024-25** presented in **July 2024**, building upon the foundations laid in the **2023** budget speeches.

questions.question: Which award did Pakistani cricketer Sana Mir receive in June 2025?

options.text: Asia Woman Cricketer of the Year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ICC Hall of Fame**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legendary Pakistani cricketer **Sana Mir** was inducted into the **ICC Hall of Fame** in **June 2025**, recognizing her immense contribution to the sport.
 
• She became one of the few women cricketers from **Pakistan** to receive this ultimate honor from the **International Cricket Council (ICC)**.
 
• **Sana Mir** served as the **captain** of the **Pakistan women's national cricket team** in both **One Day Internationals (ODIs)** and **T20Is**, leading the team with distinction for many years.
 
• In **October 2018**, she achieved the milestone of becoming the **No. 1 ODI bowler** in the **ICC Player Rankings**, which was a historic first for any woman cricketer from her country.
 
• The **ICC Hall of Fame** award is reserved for players who have demonstrated exceptional skills, character, and impact on the game over a long period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Career Profile and Background:**
 
 
• **Sana Mir** was born on **5 January 1986** in **Abbottabad**, **Pakistan**.
 
• She made her international debut in **2005** in an **ODI** against **Sri Lanka** in **Karachi**.
 
• Over her career, she played **120 ODIs** and **106 T20Is**, becoming a cornerstone of the national side.
 
 
 
• **Major Achievements and Statistics:**
 
 
• She was the first Pakistani woman to take **100 wickets** in **ODIs**, eventually finishing her career with **151 wickets** in the format.
 
• Under her **captaincy**, **Pakistan** won two **Gold Medals** at the **Asian Games** in **2010** (Guangzhou) and **2014** (Incheon).
 
• She is also known for her batting, scoring over **1,600 runs** in **ODIs** and nearly **800 runs** in **T20Is** as an all-rounder.
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement and Influence:**
 
 
• She announced her **retirement** from international cricket in **April 2020** after a **15-year** long career.
 
• Following her playing days, she has remained active in the sport as a member of the **ICC Women’s Committee** and has gained popularity as a **cricket commentator** and analyst.
 
• In **2019**, she was awarded the **Asia Game Changer Award** by the **Asia Society** for her role in empowering women through sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the ICC Hall of Fame:** The **ICC Hall of Fame** was launched in **2009** in association with the **Federation of International Cricketers' Associations (FICA)**. It celebrates the greatest icons of cricket history.
 
• **Linguistic and Cultural Impact:** **Sana Mir** is often credited with changing the perception of women's sports in **Pakistan**, encouraging a new generation of girls to take up cricket professionally.
 
• **Global Standing:** At the time of her **retirement**, she was among the top 10 most successful bowlers in **women's ODI history**.

questions.question: Why was Acko General Insurance fined ₹1 crore by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments to an unregistered intermediary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)** imposed a significant monetary penalty of **₹1 crore** on **Acko General Insurance** in **May 2025**.
 
• The penalty was levied following a regulatory investigation that uncovered **violations related to payments made to an unregistered intermediary**. According to **IRDAI** regulations, insurance companies are prohibited from transacting or paying commissions to entities that do not hold a valid license to act as an insurance intermediary.
 
• Investigations revealed that the company had entered into arrangements where payouts were channeled to entities that were not authorized under the **IRDAI (Registration of Insurance Marketing Firms) Regulations** or the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• The regulatory body observed that such practices bypass the transparent commission structures mandated for the industry and can lead to higher costs for policyholders. ***Hence, the primary reason for the fine was payments to an unregistered intermediary.***
 
• This enforcement action is part of **IRDAI's** broader mandate to maintain market discipline and ensure that all stakeholders in the insurance distribution chain are properly regulated and accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India):**
 
 
• It is a statutory body formed under the **IRDA Act, 1999**. It serves as the apex regulatory authority for the insurance sector in **India**.
 
• Headquartered in **Hyderabad**, its primary objectives include protecting the interests of policyholders and regulating, promoting, and ensuring the orderly growth of the insurance industry.
 
 
 
• **Acko General Insurance:**
 
 
• Founded in **2016** by **Varun Dua**, it is a prominent **Insurtech** company in **India** that follows a direct-to-consumer model.
 
• The company specializes in **digital-first** insurance products, including motor, health, and electronics insurance, often leveraging data and technology to offer competitive premiums.
 
 
 
• **Insurance Intermediaries:**
 
 
• These include agents, brokers, corporate agents, and web aggregators who act as a bridge between the insurance company and the customer.
 
• Under **Section 42** of the **Insurance Act, 1938**, no person can act as an intermediary or receive remuneration for procuring insurance business unless they are registered with the **IRDAI**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Insurance Act, 1938:** This is the cornerstone legislation for insurance in **India**. **Section 40** of this Act specifically prohibits the payment of any commission or brokerage to any person for soliciting or procuring insurance business in **India**, unless that person is an authorized agent or intermediary.
 
• **Regulatory Compliance:** **IRDAI** conducts periodic inspections and **audits** of insurance firms. Non-compliance with the **Expenses of Management (EoM)** limits or unauthorized payouts often results in stiff penalties, as seen in the **2025** ruling against **Acko**.
 
• **Solvency Ratio:** While not the reason for this specific fine, **IRDAI** mandates a minimum **solvency ratio** of **1.5 (150%)** for all insurers to ensure they have sufficient capital to settle claims even during financial stress.
 
• **Impact of Penalties:** Fines of this nature serve as a deterrent to other players in the **Insurtech** and traditional insurance space, emphasizing that digital innovation must go hand-in-hand with strict **regulatory compliance**.

questions.question: Who among the following chaired the Parliamentary Consultative Committee meeting on ‘Disaster Management and Capacity Building’ in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amit Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, **Shri Amit Shah**, chaired the meeting of the **Parliamentary Consultative Committee** attached to the **Ministry of Home Affairs** in **August 2025**.
 
• The primary theme of the meeting was **‘Disaster Management and Capacity Building’**, reflecting India's commitment to strengthening its resilience against natural and man-made calamities.
 
• During the meeting, **Amit Shah** highlighted the significant shift in India's approach from a **relief-centric** to a **proactive and early warning-based** disaster management strategy.
 
• The committee discussed the progress of various initiatives like the **Aapda Mitra scheme**, which aims to train **community volunteers** in disaster-prone districts across the country.
 
• He emphasized the government’s vision of **"Zero Casualty"** during disasters, citing the successful evacuation and management strategies employed during recent **cyclones** and **floods**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary Consultative Committees:**
 
 
• These committees are constituted by the **Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs** and provide a forum for **informal discussions** between Ministers and **Members of Parliament (MPs)** on the policies and working of various Ministries.
 
• Unlike Standing Committees, their meetings are usually held during **Parliament sessions** and inter-session periods to facilitate a direct exchange of ideas.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Disaster Management:**
 
 
• The **MHA** is the nodal ministry in India for managing **natural disasters** (except droughts, which fall under the Ministry of Agriculture).
 
• It oversees the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** and the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**.
 
 
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF):**
 
 
• The **NDRF** is a specialized force constituted under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, for the purpose of specialist response to a threatening disaster situation.
 
• As of **2025**, the force has been expanded with more **battalions** and advanced **technological equipment** to reduce response time during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Capacity Building Initiatives:**
 
 
• Capacity building involves **training**, **resource mobilization**, and **infrastructure development**.
 
• The **National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM)** plays a crucial role in providing **training** and **capacity building** programs for officials and stakeholders at the **national, state, and district levels**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, remains the foundational legal framework for disaster governance in India, establishing the **National, State, and District Disaster Management Authorities**.
 
• Financial support for disaster activities is managed through the **National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)** and the **State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)**, with the **15th Finance Commission** introducing a specific **Mitigation Fund**.
 
• The **August 2025** meeting also touched upon the use of **Space Technology** and **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** for **Early Warning Systems (EWS)** to provide accurate and timely alerts to the **common citizens**.
 
• **Amit Shah** reiterated that India is aiming to become a global leader in **disaster risk reduction**, aligning with the **Sendai Framework** for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030.

questions.question: According to the October 2025 Monetary Policy Report of the Reserve Bank of India, the revised GDP growth forecast for India for FY 2025–26 is _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Monetary Policy Report** released by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **October 2025**, the revised **GDP growth forecast** for India for the **Financial Year 2025–26** has been projected at **6.8%**.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which is responsible for fixing the benchmark interest rates in India, revised these growth estimates based on a comprehensive assessment of the **macroeconomic outlook** and **global economic trends**.
 
• The **real GDP growth** projection of **6.8%** reflects the resilience of the **Indian economy**, driven by robust **domestic demand**, improving **private investment**, and sustained **government capital expenditure**.
 
• The report indicates that the **services sector** and **manufacturing activity** remain the primary engines of growth, while the **agricultural sector** is expected to benefit from favorable **monsoon conditions** in the preceding year.
 
• The **RBI** utilizes sophisticated **economic modeling** and **high-frequency indicators** to arrive at these projections, ensuring that the monetary policy stance remains aligned with the objective of maintaining **price stability** while supporting growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):** 
 
 
• Established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, it serves as India's **central bank** and regulatory body for the banking system.
 
• Its primary functions include the **issuance of currency**, managing **foreign exchange reserves**, and acting as a **banker to the government** and other banks.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):** 
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member committee** constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Governor of the RBI** and meets at least **four times a year** to decide on the **policy repo rate** required to achieve the **inflation target**.
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):** 
 
 
• **GDP** is the total **monetary or market value** of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, typically a **financial year**.
 
• In India, the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, is responsible for calculating and releasing GDP data.
 
 
 
• **Financial Year in India:** 
 
 
• The **Financial Year (FY)** in India begins on **April 1** and ends on **March 31** of the following calendar year. Therefore, **FY 2025–26** covers the period from **April 2025 to March 2026**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **October 2025 report** factors in several **global risks**, including **geopolitical tensions**, **volatility in global commodity prices**, and the **monetary policy actions** of major central banks like the **US Federal Reserve**.
 
• The **output gap**—the difference between **actual output** and **potential output**—is a key metric monitored by the **RBI** to determine if the economy is operating at full capacity without generating excessive **inflation**.
 
• The **6.8% growth** target is supported by a significant increase in **bank credit growth** and healthy **corporate balance sheets**, which encourage fresh **capacity expansion** (Capex) by the private sector.
 
• **Inflation targeting** remains a core focus of the RBI, with a medium-term target of **4%** within a band of **+/- 2%**, as per the **flexible inflation targeting framework** adopted in **2016**.

questions.question: In the 2025 Kho Kho World Cup, the Indian men’s team secured the first-ever championship title by defeating which opponent in the final match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• This victory marks a significant milestone for the sport of **Kho Kho**, as it was the **inaugural edition** of the global championship, aimed at promoting this traditional Indian sport on an international platform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Double Glory for India**:
 
 
• Apart from the men's team, the **Indian women’s team** also secured the championship title by defeating **Nepal** in their respective final.
 
• The women's team won by an **innings and 13 points** with a final score of **33-20**, completing a historic **double gold** for the host nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which among the following organisations launched the ‘Scheme for Promoting Registration of Employers and Employees’ (SPREE 2025)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Employees' State Insurance Corporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)** launched the **‘Scheme for Promoting Registration of Employers and Employees’ (SPREE 2025)** to enhance the coverage of social security benefits.
 
• The main objective of **SPREE 2025** is to encourage **employers** to register themselves and their **employees** who were previously eligible but remained unregistered under the **ESI Act, 1948**.
 
• The scheme is designed as a **one-time opportunity** for **employers** to come forward and formalize their workforce without the immediate burden of past penalties, thereby promoting **ease of doing business**.
 
• The duration of this scheme is set for **six months**, specifically remaining operational from **October 2024** to **March 2025**.
 
• By registering under this scheme, **employees** gain access to a wide array of **social security** benefits, including comprehensive **medical care** and **cash benefits** during contingencies like sickness or injury.
 
• This initiative is a strategic step by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** to ensure the **formalization** of the Indian workforce and provide a safety net to those in the organized and semi-organized sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Act, 1948:**
 
 
• It was the first major **social security** legislation in independent **India**, designed to provide **health insurance** and **disability benefits** to workers.
 
• The **ESIC** is a **statutory body** established under this Act and functions under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Labour and Employment**, Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Contribution Rates:**
 
 
• The **ESI Scheme** is self-financing, where contributions are made by both the **employer** and the **employee**.
 
• Currently, the **employer's contribution** is **3.25%** and the **employee's contribution** is **0.75%** of the total wages paid.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• The Act applies to **factories** and other establishments like **shops, hotels, restaurants, cinemas,** and **private medical institutions** employing **10 or more** persons.
 
• The current **wage ceiling** for coverage under the **ESI Scheme** is **Rs. 21,000** per month (**Rs. 25,000** for persons with disabilities).
 
 
 
• **Types of Benefits provided by ESIC:**
 
 
• **Medical Benefit:** Full medical care is provided to an **Insured Person** and their family members from the day they enter insurable employment.
 
• **Sickness Benefit:** Periodic payments to any **insured person** in case of sickness certified by a medical practitioner.
 
• **Maternity Benefit:** Payable to **insured women** for confinement or miscarriage, generally for a period of **26 weeks**.
 
• **Disablement Benefit:** Provided to employees who suffer **employment injury** resulting in temporary or permanent disability.
 
• **Dependants' Benefit:** Paid in the form of a **monthly pension** to the dependants of a deceased **Insured Person** in cases where death occurs due to **employment injury** or occupational hazards.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **ESIC** headquarters is located in **New Delhi**, and it manages a vast network of **hospitals** and **dispensaries** across the **country**.
 
• Digital integration through the **Shram Suvidha Portal** and the issuance of **Pehchan Cards** (identity cards) has streamlined the process of availing **cashless medical services**.
 
• The **Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (ABVKY)** is another significant welfare scheme under **ESIC** that provides **unemployment allowance** to insured persons who have lost their jobs.

questions.question: What was the esteemed category of civilian honours conferred upon legendary Indian hockey player PR Sreejesh by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Awards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PR Sreejesh**, the veteran goalkeeper of the **Indian Men’s Hockey Team**, was conferred with the **Padma Shri** (which falls under the **Padma Awards** category) for his distinguished service in the field of **Sports**.
 
• The honor was presented by **President Droupadi Murmu** during a civil investiture ceremony held at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** in **April 2025**.
 
• Sreejesh is widely recognized as one of the greatest goalkeepers in the history of hockey, often referred to as **"The Wall"** for his exceptional reflexes and leadership on the field.
 
• He played a pivotal role in ending India's 41-year Olympic medal drought by helping the team secure the **Bronze Medal** at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics** and subsequently defending the title at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• The **Padma Awards** are one of the highest civilian honors of the country, announced annually on the eve of **Republic Day** (January 26th).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PR Sreejesh's Accolades:**
 
 
• Before the Padma Shri, he was honored with the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **2021**, which is India's highest sporting honor.
 
• He was also the recipient of the **Arjuna Award** in **2015** and was named the **World Games Athlete of the Year 2021**, becoming only the second Indian to win this global award.
 
• Hailing from **Kerala**, he served as the **Captain** of the Indian national team during the **2016 Rio Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **The Padma Awards:**
 
 
• Instituted in **1954**, these awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (distinguished service of high order), and **Padma Shri** (distinguished service in any field).
 
• The awards seek to recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved, such as **Art, Social Work, Public Affairs, Science and Engineering, Trade and Industry, Medicine, Literature and Education, Sports, and Civil Service**.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Awards:**
 
 
• These are separate from civilian honors and include the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna**, **Arjuna Award**, **Dronacharya Award** (for coaches), and **Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime Achievement**.
 
• These are usually conferred by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** on **National Sports Day** (August 29).
 
 
 
• **Bharat Ratna:**
 
 
• This is the **highest civilian award** of the **Republic of India**. It is awarded in recognition of exceptional service/performance of the highest order in any field of human endeavor.

questions.question: India's SDG ranking in the 10th Sustainable Development Report was released by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report (SDR)**, which includes the **SDG Index** and **Dashboards**, is a global assessment of countries' progress towards achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• This report is released annually by the **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 2.***
 
• The **SDSN** has been publishing these reports since **2016** (with earlier iterations dating back to the adoption of the goals), and the **2024** edition marks the **9th** global edition, while the **10th** anniversary of the **SDSN** itself or specific regional versions often lead to the "10th" nomenclature in various academic contexts.
 
• The report provides a **score (0–100)** for each country, representing the percentage of **SDG** achievement. A score of **100** indicates that all targets have been met.
 
• It uses a **"traffic light"** system (green, yellow, orange, red) in its **Dashboards** to help countries identify where they are lagging and where they are making progress across the **17 Goals**.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Solutions Network** operates under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** and was established in **2012**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):**
 
 
• The **WEF** is an international non-governmental organization based in **Cologny, Switzerland**, founded by **Klaus Schwab** in **1971**.
 
• It is famous for its annual meeting in **Davos** and releases reports such as the **Global Gender Gap Report**, **Global Competitiveness Report**, and **Global Risks Report**.
 
• It does not release the primary global **SDG Index**.
 
 
 
• **World Bank Report:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to the governments of low- and middle-income countries.
 
• Its flagship publication is the **World Development Report (WDR)**, which focuses on a different aspect of development each year (e.g., **Digital Dividends**, **Governance and the Law**).
 
• While it provides data for the **SDGs**, it is not the publisher of the **Sustainable Development Report**.
 
 
 
• **International Monetary Fund (IMF) Report:**
 
 
• The **IMF** focuses on global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and international trade.
 
• Major reports include the **World Economic Outlook (WEO)**, **Global Financial Stability Report**, and **Fiscal Monitor**.
 
• The **IMF** monitors macroeconomic health rather than specific **SDG** indicator rankings.
 
 
 
• **The 17 SDGs:**
 
 
• Adopted by all **193 United Nations Member States** in **September 2015** as part of the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**.
 
• Key goals include **Goal 1: No Poverty**, **Goal 5: Gender Equality**, **Goal 13: Climate Action**, and **Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SDSN Leadership:** The **SDSN** is currently led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs**, a world-renowned economist and expert in sustainable development.
 
• **Data Sources:** The report relies heavily on official data from the **United Nations**, **World Bank**, **World Health Organization (WHO)**, and **International Labour Organization (ILO)**, as well as non-official data where gaps exist.
 
• **India's Context:** In the **Sustainable Development Report 2024**, **India** was ranked **109th** out of **166** countries with a score of approximately **64.0**. The country has shown progress in goals like **Climate Action** and **Responsible Consumption** but faces challenges in **Zero Hunger (Goal 2)** and **Gender Equality (Goal 5)**.
 
• **Spillover Index:** A unique feature of the **SDSN** report is the **Spillover Index**, which measures the positive and negative effects one country has on another's ability to achieve the **SDGs** (e.g., through trade, security, or environmental impacts).
